what_happened: An operator redid a hand revert of an earlier landing. The second revert brought back a test that pins the digest of the reading-inputs file (athena.toml). That test fails on any change to athena.toml, including the exemption the revert shipped with. CI failed on a 13-minute run. No job was rejected. The mistake cost one more CI round.
cause: Athena has no revert command that checks the result before it is pushed. A hand revert silently restores old tests along with old content, and CI is the first place the restored tests run against the current files. A second cause is that tests which pin the digest of a file meant to change, such as athena.toml, fail on any legitimate edit. They are brittle by design, and nothing in the repo flags or removes them. The earlier revert case failed on the history check in the same way, late in CI.
prevention: Add an `athena revert` command that keeps append-only records. Before it lets the result be pushed, it should run the repo's full test suite and the history check locally on the reverted tree, and refuse on any failure. Separately, replace the pinned reading-inputs digest test with a check that does not break on legitimate athena.toml edits. A scan should list any other tests that pin digests of files expected to change.
proposed_request: Add an `athena revert <landing>` command that reverts a landing while keeping append-only records. Before it finishes, it must run the repo's full test suite and the full history check on the reverted tree. It must refuse and print the failing tests if any fail, so a revert is never pushed red. Also find every test that pins a digest or fixed value derived from a file Athena expects to change, starting with the reading-inputs digest test on athena.toml. Change each so that a legitimate edit to that file does not fail it, while a real unintended change still does. Acceptance: reverting a sample landing that restores the pinned digest test is refused locally with the failing test named. After the fix, an unrelated athena.toml edit does not break any test.
